ruledOut: Model price as the main lever
Fan-out concurrency as the cause of the quota failure

label: The 24-iteration ceiling is unreachable at the measured 8-11 minutes per iteration under the default 120-minute duration budget; the duration stop binds near iteration 11-15, and one archive run already raised the budget to 360 minutes for 10 iterations.

Setup costs 3-10 minutes per lineage before iteration 1 (createdAt to first iteration), and a fan-out pays it per lineage although the root has already resolved the topic and partitioned the frontier.

The fixed 50/35/15 split gives a three-node review exactly 12 depth-1 iterations at a 24 cap, which is exactly the 3 nodes x 4 dimensions cost, leaving zero growth; the protocol pushes the doubling arithmetic onto the operator.
Per-iteration cost is dominated by cache re-read of unchanged context (6.2M cache-read vs 0.33M input per iteration), and the prompt pack restates the full topic and state summary every iteration.

No host-measured durationMs reaches the iteration record, so latency claims rest on model-written timestamps that mix queue, model and idle time even though fanout-run already computes slotDurationMs.

question: Do the dispatch receipts under each lineage carry slotDurationMs, and can that field be joined to the iteration row to separate model time from queue time in the archive runs?
What is the measured setup time per executor kind, and does skipping the context ladder in a fan-out child actually remove it?

direction: Treating model price as the main cost lever
reason: The measured cost is dominated by cache-read of unchanged context and by wall-clock latency, so a cheaper model changes the multiplier rather than the shape.
